title: Streaming handshake defer and error-tiering for JSON response contracts
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: Structured-output users expect both low-latency streaming and strict JSON schema guarantees. Previously our runtime attempted to validate schema progressively which led to false-positive schema errors on partial streams and confusing client behavior during function/tool calls. Motivation: provide a mechanism that preserves streaming responsiveness while avoiding premature schema failures and improving actionable error messages and telemetry for regressions. This PR introduces a deferred handshake mode for response_format=schema where schema enforcement is anchored to checkpoints (handshake points) rather than token-level partial validation. It also adds an error-tiering model that maps validation failures to user-facing error codes, SDK hints, and internal telemetry severities. Summary of changes: 1) New streaming handshake: the runtime delays strict schema enforcement until one of three conditions is met: explicit end-of-object token, a checkpoint token emitted by the generator, or a configurable timeout/size threshold. This prevents spurious schema failures on partial sequence fragments. 2) Checkpoint tokens and resume metadata: introduce a lightweight checkpoint token in the stream (internal token that is dropped by OpenAI-compat adapter) and a resume token that lets client SDKs request a schema revalidation or stream resume without reissuing the entire prompt. 3) Error-tiering: validation results are classified into tiers (soft-warning, recoverable-failure, hard-failure). Soft warnings are surfaced in metadata with suggested SDK coercion hints; recoverable failures trigger a stream fallback to permissive coercion or canonicalization; hard failures cause stream termination with an explicit error code and suggested remediation. 4) OpenAI adapter changes: add compatibility layer to strip internal checkpoint markers and translate engine error codes into openai-compatible error shapes. 5) Tool/function-call safety: tool-call fencing ensures that a partially validated structured tool call is not executed; instead the call is buffered until a checkpoint confirms schema conformance or the runtime falls back to permissive mode with explicit logs. 6) Telemetry and debugging: new telemetry fields for validation_tier, handshake_latency_ms and resume_attempts; improved human-readable diagnostics in logs. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed by runtime and SDK owners - [x] Automated unit + integration tests - [x] SDK hint surface added to Python/TS SDKs - [x] Docs updated with handshake behavior and migration guidance - [x] E2E Canary on perf-canary with synthetic streaming workload

Notes: This description consolidates implementation details and operational guidance for reviewers. See commits summary for granular changes and test fixture examples.
commits: 5 commits: 1) introduce handshake infrastructure and checkpoint token emitter; 2) add schema-tier validator and mapping logic; 3) openai adapter translation + tests; 4) toolcall fencing and buffering; 5) docs and SDK hint strings. Each commit includes unit tests and changelog entries.
summary_of_changes: Implements deferred schema handshake for streaming structured output, introduces checkpoint/resume tokens, introduces validation tiers and operator-facing error codes, fences tool calls until schema confirmation, updates OpenAI adapter to remain compatible, includes SDK hints and docs.
review_conversation: Luis Gomez: Nice approach to avoiding premature validation. A couple of nits on the timeout defaults and telemetry cardinality.
Maya Chen: Responding — lowered default handshake timeout from 800ms to 500ms after perf canary, added sampling to handshake telemetry to avoid high-cardinality in high-throughput customers.
Ravi Patel: Question on toolcall fencing: what happens for long-running tools? Can we timebox buffered calls?
Maya Chen: We added a max-buffer-duration config per flow; if exceeded we emit a recoverable-failure and surface SDK hint to either retry or accept permissive coercion. Added tests for that behavior.
Sophie Nguyen: Docs look good; add migration note for customers that relied on token-level validation errors.
Maya Chen: Added migration guidance and a flag to enable legacy token-level validation for customers who opt in.
Luis Gomez: Approving pending one small logging comment fix.
Maya Chen: Fixed logging format; squashed commits and pushed final changes.
release_notes: Added deferred streaming handshake for structured responses: reduces false-positive schema failures during streaming, improves compatibility with function/tool calls, and provides clearer error tiers and SDK hints. Configuration: handshake.timeout_ms (default 500), validation.mode (strict|deferred|permissive).
notes_for_ops: Canary results show median handshake latency added ~8ms and 95th percentile ~35ms under synthetic bursts. Default settings should be safe for existing SLAs. Operators can tune handshake.timeout_ms and validation.mode per model route. Enable sampling for validation telemetry to avoid high-cardinality metrics.
egress_compatibility_notes: OpenAI adapter strips internal checkpoint tokens and maps our validation_tier into openai.error.type and error.message fields. Older clients will see a permissive fallback message; upgrade SDKs to receive resume tokens and structured hints.
post_merge_tasks: 1) Monitor new telemetry: validation_tier and handshake_latency_ms for customer routes; 2) Announce migration and opt-in legacy flag in customer changelog; 3) Coordinate SDK releases (python + ts) to surface resume API and hints; 4) Backport cherry-pick to release/2026-02 for hotfix channel.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: increased telemetry cardinality and slight added latency on handshake. Mitigation: telemetry sampling, conservative default timeout, and canary rollout by default. Also provided opt-out (legacy_token_validation=true) for customers that require prior behavior.
test_plan: Unit tests for validator tiers and fencing, integration tests for stream resume and toolcall buffering, canary e2e with perf-canary using 10k synthetic streams, compatibility tests against openai-adapter contract. All tests run in CI and passed.
note_on_privacy: No customer data surfaced in telemetry; resume tokens are opaque handles. Documented guidelines enforced in observability/telemetry/validation_metrics_schema.yaml.
